question: Tang's Laplace floor is Lambda(f) > 2 for every admissible f. Is there an analogous floor at the matched level under modified-Helmholtz degradation?
supersedes: floor-under-degradation.txt — that run thresholded at the field value at the ORIGIN, which is the critical level only when every root lies exactly on the unit circle; for interior roots |f(0)| < 1 so it measured a different set and reported Lambda = 0.50 at Da = 0.

threshold_derivation.laplace: {|f|<1} <=> sum log|z-z_i| < 0 <=> c > 0, c = -sum log|z-z_i|. Level FIXED at 0 regardless of where the roots are.
threshold_derivation.limit: c_Da(z) -> -sum_i log|z - z_i| + n*(log(2/sqrt(Da)) - gamma) as Da -> 0
threshold_derivation.matched_level: L(n, Da) = n*(log(2/sqrt(Da)) - gamma); then {c_Da > L} -> {|f| < 1}
threshold_derivation.domain_of_validity: bounded iff L > 0 iff sqrt(Da) < 2 e^{-gamma} iff Da < Da*
threshold_derivation.containment_radius: c_Da(z) <= n K_0((|z|-1) sqrt(Da)) for |z|>1 => set lies in |z| < 1 + t/sqrt(Da) with K_0(t) = L/n (brentq); half-width 1.03x.

instrument_limit.finding: Lambda measured on a pixel lattice at the exact level |f| = 1 is NOT reliable when three or more components pinch at one point. Refinement does not fix it; the sub-cell offset changes the answer by factors of 2 to 7.
instrument_limit.example: Lambda(z^8 - 1): 18.77 / 2.35 / 2.35 / 7.06 / 2.35 across lattice variants; closed form 2.364444. Lambda(z^5 - 1) worsens from 5.20 to 10.40 on refinement from n_grid 1201 to 4001.
instrument_limit.cause: f = z^n - 1 has f' = n z^{n-1}, one critical point at the origin of multiplicity n-1 with |f(0)| = 1, so all n petals pinch there and 2n sectors meet at a point; 4-connectivity resolves that only by lattice accident.
instrument_limit.consequence: such configurations are DETECTED and excluded, not silently averaged in

guards.A: exact critical points of f on the level set (Laplace)
guards.A_prime: k-fold rotational symmetry with k >= 3 (all Da; kernel-independent)
guards.B: agreement of Lambda across 3 lattice variants to 1.0%

method.reported_Lambda: median over lattice variants; the FLOOR test uses the MINIMUM over variants, which is the conservative direction

per_damkohler.reason: L = n*(log(2/sqrt(Da)) - gamma) <= 0 while c_Da > 0 everywhere, so {c_Da > L} is the whole plane; Da >= Da* = 1.2609470067

verdict: FLOOR HOLDS at every non-degenerate Damkohler tested (Da in [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0]). Global minimum Lambda = 3.708436 at n02_roots_of_unity, Da = 0.0, re-verified at h/2 and h/2.5. Da = [4.0] is DEGENERATE — past Da* = 1.260947 the matched level is non-positive and {c_Da > L} is the whole plane, so the question is EMPTY there, not answered. This is a bounded numerical sweep over 80 configurations, not a proof; it is evidence for an analogue of Tang's floor, not a demonstration of one.
